title: Photosynthesis, Respiration and the Carbon Cycle
short: Photosynthesis pulls CO₂ from the air into sugars; respiration by plants, animals and decomposers returns it. Their balance, along with burning and the ocean, sets the carbon dioxide in the air.
trouble: Students think plants only photosynthesize and animals only respire. Plants respire all the time too; over a whole day a growing plant takes in more CO₂ than it gives off.

blocks.html: Put Photosynthesis and Cellular Respiration side by side and they look like mirror images. The products of one are the raw materials of the other, and together they move carbon around the planet.

Photosynthesis pulls CO₂ from the air into sugars. Respiration by plants, animals and decomposers returns it. Their balance, along with burning fuels and exchange with the ocean, sets the amount of carbon dioxide in the air.

blocks.name: bi-energy
blocks.cap: The cycle: the chloroplast's outputs are the mitochondrion's inputs, and the other way around. Energy enters as light and leaves as heat; matter goes around.

blocks.name: bi-cycle
blocks.cap: The carbon cycle. Tap a process to see where it moves carbon.

blocks.html: Plants have mitochondria too, and they respire all day and all night to power their own cells. In the light, a growing plant photosynthesizes faster than it respires, so overall it takes in CO₂ and gives off O₂. In the dark it only respires, so it gives off CO₂. What a gas sensor measures in the light is the net rate: $$\text{net uptake} = \text{gross photosynthesis} - \text{respiration}$$ Over a whole day, a growing plant takes in more CO₂ than it gives off; the extra carbon becomes its new leaves, stems and roots.

blocks.title: Gross from net
blocks.q: In the light, a plant takes up 40 mg of CO₂ per hour (net). In the dark it gives off 10 mg per hour. What is its gross rate of photosynthesis?
steps: Respiration runs in the light too, at about the dark rate: 10 mg per hour.
Gross = net + respiration $= 40 + 10 = 50$ mg per hour.

blocks.title: A whole day
blocks.q: The same plant gets 12 hours of light and 12 hours of dark. What is its net CO₂ uptake for the day?
steps: Net: $480 - 120 = 360$ mg taken up: the plant grows.

blocks.html: Thinking plants only photosynthesize and animals only respire. Every living cell respires, plant cells included, day and night. Plants simply photosynthesize faster than they respire when the light is good, so their net exchange in the light is CO₂ in and O₂ out.
